boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Dickinson College
boards.description: When the Waidner-Spahr Library sessions stretch late, Dickinsonians rely on a mix of on-campus hubs and local Carlisle staples. From the classic 'Hotchee' dog to 24-hour convenience runs, these spots define the after-hours experience in this historic college town.

cards.title: Union Station
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Campus Hub
cards.notes: Located in the Holland Union Building, this is the primary spot for late-night burgers and specialty sandwiches using meal plan points.
cards.short_summary: The central on-campus dining option for students seeking hot food and snacks until late in the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Union Station is located in the upper level of the Holland Union Building and is conveniently open from breakfast until late at night.
cards.source_title: Union Station Hours & Menu - Carlisle - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM most weeknights during the academic semester.

cards.title: The Juice Bar at Underground
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Smoothies & Sushi
cards.notes: Found in the Underground Student Lounge, it offers a healthier late-night alternative with smoothies and fresh sushi.
cards.short_summary: A student lounge cafe providing organic coffee, fresh juices, and sushi for late-night study breaks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Underground Student Lounge featuring The Juice Bar... serves organically grown fair-trade coffees, fruit and vegetable juice, made-to-order smoothies, teas and sushi.
cards.source_title: Campus Dining Locations - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Typically open until 10:00 PM or 11:00 PM on weeknights.

cards.title: Devil's Den
cards.subtitle: Campus Convenience Store
cards.notes: The go-to for dorm room essentials, snacks, and groceries located in the lower level of the HUB.
cards.short_summary: A campus convenience store stocked with snacks, produce, and pantry staples for late-night needs.
cards.evidence_claim: Devils Den has snacks and groceries, including fresh produce, fresh meats, cheeses, fresh dairy, a frozen aisle, and a pantry aisle.
cards.source_title: Campus Dining Locations - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM daily during the school year.

cards.title: Carlisle Diner
cards.subtitle: Classic 24/7 Diner
cards.notes: A local staple for all-day breakfast and late-night comfort food, popular for post-event gatherings.
cards.short_summary: A traditional family diner offering late-night dining and breakfast favorites 24 hours a day.
cards.evidence_claim: Late night dining and all day breakfast offerings make us your one-stop shop for the best food in Carlisle!
cards.source_title: Carlisle Diner: Home
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Hamilton Restaurant
cards.subtitle: Home of the Hotchee Dog
cards.notes: Famous for its 'Hotchee' dogs, this historic spot is a must-visit for students exploring downtown Carlisle.
cards.short_summary: A Greek-owned local favorite since the 1920s, known for its signature hot dogs and Greek salads.
cards.evidence_claim: Greek owned local favorite since 1920s and award winner for best hot dogs; try their famous 'hotchee' dog.
cards.source_title: Dining - The Carlisle House
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:00 PM or 9:30 PM; a classic 'early' late-night stop.

cards.title: Sheetz on Harrisburg Pike
cards.subtitle: 24/7 MTO Run
cards.notes: The essential 24-hour run for 'Made-To-Order' food, from appetizer samplers to breakfast burritos.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 convenience destination for students with cars or using delivery for late-night MTO snacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Made-To-Order® food and beverages 24/7/365.
cards.source_title: Sheetz
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours, 365 days a year.

cards.title: Denny's
cards.subtitle: The 24-Hour Grand Slam
cards.notes: A reliable off-campus destination for late-night breakfast and burgers when campus options are closed.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour diner serving breakfast, burgers, and milkshakes at any hour of the night.
cards.evidence_claim: From 24 hour breakfast in Carlisle to late night food in Carlisle, we serve pancakes, Grand Slams, burgers, and breakfast sandwiches 24/7.
cards.source_title: Diner Favorites - Denny's
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Cravings
cards.notes: Located on East High Street, this is a frequent stop for quick, late-night tacos and burritos.
cards.short_summary: A popular fast-food choice for students seeking late-night meals near the downtown area.
cards.evidence_claim: Find Taco Bell for dinner near you at 401 East High Street in Carlisle, PA... Open til 1:00 AM.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell® Dinner Near Me in Carlisle, PA
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru typically open until 1:00 AM or later.

cards.title: McDonald's
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Golden Arches
cards.notes: A convenient stop on East High Street for late-night fries and burgers, often accessible via drive-thru.
cards.short_summary: A standard late-night fast food option for students located just east of the main campus area.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald's at 608 E High, Carlisle, PA... Open now [late night].
cards.source_title: McDonald's | Carlisle PA
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open late; hours vary by day.

cards.title: Miseno II Pizzeria
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Pizza Slices
cards.notes: Located on West High Street, it's a prime spot for a quick slice of pizza or an Italian sub.
cards.short_summary: A local pizzeria offering slices and Italian favorites within walking distance of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Miseno II Pizzeria & Italian - Carlisle, PA - 598 W High St - Hours, Menu, Order.
cards.source_title: Best Pizza by the slice in Carlisle, PA | Miseno Pizza and Ristorante
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:30 PM or 10:00 PM; a popular evening dinner-to-late-night transition spot.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional student spaces and quiet corners of Dickinson College that go beyond the standard admissions route, from specialized reading rooms to newly renovated hubs.

cards.title: Upper Level Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Quiet enclosed spaces with tech integration
cards.notes: Reserve one of 13 enclosed rooms for group work; upper-level spots include flat panel monitors and USB-C connectivity for collaborative projects.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed group study rooms in the main library equipped with collaborative technology.
cards.evidence_claim: The library has 13 study rooms located on the upper, main, and lower levels, with upper and main level rooms featuring flat panel monitors and USB-C capability.
cards.source_title: Study Room Use & Reservation Guidelines - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Reservations must be made 8 hours in advance; sessions last up to three hours per day.

cards.title: Tome Science Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Second floor specialized library
cards.notes: Visit the second floor for a quiet atmosphere surrounded by physics and math journals; it offers large windows with views of the academic quad.
cards.short_summary: A specialized reading room on the second floor of Tome Hall focused on science and mathematics.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tome Science Reading Room is located on the second floor of Tome and is open to students, staff, and faculty at all times for consulting specialized journals.
cards.source_title: Tome Science Reading Room | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Open to students, staff, and faculty at all times.

cards.title: Rector Interaction Spaces
cards.subtitle: Collaborative nooks in the science wing
cards.notes: Utilize the modern 'interaction spaces' designed for interdisciplinary work; these comfortable seating areas are popular for impromptu study sessions.
cards.short_summary: Modern collaborative work and study spaces integrated throughout the Rector Science Complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rector Science Complex includes comfortable collaborative work and study spaces designed to bring students and professors together across disciplines.
cards.source_title: A Look Inside Dickinson College's Rector Science Complex
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; primarily used by science students but open to all.

cards.title: The HUB Underground
cards.subtitle: Lower level social and study lounge
cards.notes: Check out the new 'bed-like' seating arrangements tucked under the stairs for a relaxed, homey environment during long breaks between classes.
cards.short_summary: A newly renovated lower-level lounge area in the student union featuring unique furniture.
cards.evidence_claim: The HUB renovation introduced new student gathering areas, including large seating arrangements tucked under the stairs in the HUB Underground.
cards.source_title: Students concerned over glimpses of HUB renovations - The Dickinsonian
cards.access_notes: Open during HUB operating hours; late night access typically available during the semester.

cards.title: Althouse Hall Lounge
cards.subtitle: Quiet academic quad retreat
cards.notes: Find the lounge in Althouse Hall for a central but often quieter alternative to the library, located right on the historic academic quad.
cards.short_summary: A student lounge located within the historic Althouse Hall on the main academic quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Students identify the lounge in Althouse Hall as a favorite campus space for its location and atmosphere.
cards.source_title: Spaces We Love | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Accessible during standard academic building hours.

cards.title: Stern Great Room
cards.subtitle: Global education hub lounge
cards.notes: Relax in the Stern Great Room, a central space for the global education community that often hosts coffee hours and international events.
cards.short_summary: A large, multi-purpose room in the Stern Center used for both events and student relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stern Center includes the Stern Great Room, which is listed as a key location for campus events and student engagement.
cards.source_title: Stern Center | Locations - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Open during business hours; often used for scheduled global programming.

cards.title: Allison Hall Lounge
cards.subtitle: Expanded social and study space
cards.notes: Head to Allison Hall to find recently furnished lounge spaces that provide a more relaxed alternative to the formal Great Hall.
cards.short_summary: A furnished lounge area in Allison Hall designed to expand student social and study options.
cards.evidence_claim: Allison Hall was furnished to expand lounge space for students, providing more areas for activities and informal gathering.
cards.source_title: Allison Hall Furnished to Expand Lounge Space - The Dickinsonian
cards.access_notes: Available during building hours; check the online calendar for Great Hall events.

cards.title: Art & Art History Study Hallway
cards.subtitle: Creative corridor for art students
cards.notes: Walk through the Goodyear Building's study hallway, where art majors often gather near individual studio spaces and the student-run gallery.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated study and social corridor within the Goodyear Building art complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The Art and Art History Department facilities include an 'Art & Art History Study Hallway' in the Goodyear building alongside studio spaces.
cards.source_title: Facilities and Resources | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Art majors have 24/7 key access; general gallery access is Tuesday-Saturday afternoons.

cards.title: Kaufman Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Sustainability and earth science hub
cards.notes: Study in the Kaufman Hall Reading Room (Room 118), a quiet spot located near the Center for Sustainability Education and the Museum of Earth Sciences.
cards.short_summary: A quiet reading room located on the first floor of Kaufman Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Kaufman Hall features a dedicated Reading Room (Room 118) on its first floor plan near the Geophysics and Microscopy labs.
cards.source_title: KAUFMAN HALL Floor Plan
cards.access_notes: Accessible during academic building hours.

cards.title: The Biblio Café
cards.subtitle: Library social study spot
cards.notes: Grab a coffee and find a seat in the Biblio Café; it's the designated 'loud' study area where talking is encouraged compared to the quiet upper floors.
cards.short_summary: A social study area and café located on the main floor of the library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Biblio Café is highlighted as a favorite student spot for relaxing and having coffee within the Waidner-Spahr Library.
cards.source_title: Spaces We Love | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; café service hours may vary.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore Dickinson College and Carlisle without spending a dime. From historic campus traditions and art galleries to organic farm tours and fitness classes, these social activities are free for students and often open to the public.

cards.title: Browse the Trout Gallery
cards.subtitle: Weiss Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Visit the college's art museum to see permanent collections and rotating exhibits. It is free and open to the public Tuesday through Saturday.
cards.short_summary: The Trout Gallery is Dickinson's free art museum featuring ancient to contemporary works.
cards.evidence_claim: The Trout Gallery is free and open to the public. It is located on the Dickinson College campus in the Weiss Center for the Arts.
cards.source_title: Visit | TroutHome - The Trout Gallery
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Saturday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Free admission for all visitors.

cards.title: Walk the Old West Steps
cards.subtitle: John Dickinson Campus
cards.notes: Participate in the tradition of walking up these historic limestone steps during Convocation to ceremonially sign into the college.
cards.short_summary: Walking the Old West steps is a core Dickinson tradition for entering and graduating students.
cards.evidence_claim: During Convocation, new students walk up the steps, through the doors into Memorial Hall and sign into the college.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: The doors open twice a year for ceremonies; the steps are accessible for photos year-round.

cards.title: Tour the College Farm
cards.subtitle: 553 Park Drive, Boiling Springs
cards.notes: Take a free self-guided tour of the 80-acre organic farm during weekday working hours to see sustainable food production in action.
cards.short_summary: The Dickinson College Farm offers free self-guided tours of its organic operations during the week.
cards.evidence_claim: You may also consider taking a free self-guided tour during farm working hours, 7:30am-4:30pm Monday-Friday.
cards.source_title: Visit the Farm | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Self-guided tours available Monday-Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

cards.title: Study at Waidner-Spahr
cards.subtitle: High Street Entrance
cards.notes: Access the campus library for free until 5 p.m. daily. It offers a quiet environment for research and community study.
cards.short_summary: Waidner-Spahr Library is open to the public for study and research during daytime hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The library is open to the public until 5 p.m. each day. Current Dickinson ID is required starting at 5 p.m.
cards.source_title: General Public Hours | Library Hours - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Public access ends at 5 p.m. daily; Dickinson ID required for late-night entry.

cards.title: Join a Group Fitness Class
cards.subtitle: Kline Life/Sports Learning Center
cards.notes: Dickinson students can attend free fitness classes like yoga, Pilates, and Zumba. Sign up through the Gateway portal.
cards.short_summary: Free group fitness classes are available to all Dickinson students at the Kline Fitness Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Fitness classes are provided to all Dickinson students, faculty and staff. Classes include cardio fusion, Pilates, zumba and others.
cards.source_title: Group Fitness Classes - Carlisle - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Available to students with valid ID; registration via Totora on the Dickinson Gateway.

cards.title: Attend a Public Lecture
cards.subtitle: Allison Hall
cards.notes: Head to the Great Hall for free public readings and lectures by visiting scholars and alumni throughout the academic year.
cards.short_summary: Allison Hall hosts free public lectures and cultural events for the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: Most events are free and open to the public: stop by! ... public reading on Thursday, February 19 at 7 p.m. in Allison Great Hall.
cards.source_title: Events and Speakers | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Events are typically free and open to the public; check the campus calendar for schedules.

cards.title: Hang Out at The Quarry
cards.subtitle: College and Louther Streets
cards.notes: Use this reimagined social space for student meetings or casual hangouts. It features comfortable furniture and a cozy atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: The Quarry is a historic building converted into a free social and meeting space for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Quarry would be renovated to provide another social space for students... Cist saw the Quarry's second floor as a better spot for conversation.
cards.source_title: Few Student Groups Use Reimagined Quarry Space - The Dickinsonian
cards.access_notes: Open to students for socializing and club meetings; can be reserved via EngageD.

cards.title: Jog the Dickinson Park Trail
cards.subtitle: Dickinson Park
cards.notes: Enjoy the outdoors on the walking and jogging trail at Dickinson Park, which is free and open to the general public.
cards.short_summary: The Dickinson Park walking and jogging trail is a free outdoor recreational resource.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dickinson Park walking/jogging trail is open to the public. Note: No dogs are permitted on the trail.
cards.source_title: Dickinson Community Resources
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; no dogs allowed on the trail.

cards.title: Grab a Donut on the Plaza
cards.subtitle: Britton Plaza
cards.notes: Look for summer 'Community Donut Socials' on Tuesdays where students and staff gather for free treats and conversation.
cards.short_summary: Britton Plaza hosts free social events like donut socials for the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: Employees and students are welcome to come to the Britton Plaza each Tuesday this summer to enjoy the company of colleagues and some donuts!
cards.source_title: Events | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Typically held on Tuesday mornings during the summer; check the calendar for academic year events.

cards.title: Study in the Rector Atrium
cards.subtitle: Stuart and James Halls
cards.notes: Find a spot in the collaborative work and study spaces of this LEED-certified complex, known for its modern design and natural light.
cards.short_summary: The Rector Science Complex offers modern, free collaborative study spaces for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The complex... includes comfortable collaborative work and study spaces, making it easier to engage in interdisciplinary problem-solving.
cards.source_title: A Look Inside Dickinson College's Rector Science Complex
cards.access_notes: Open to students for study; building access may require ID after hours.

cards.short_summary: A 24-hour computer lab and study space located within the Holland Union Building.

cards.short_summary: A quiet outdoor study area with tables and chairs in front of the Stern Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The front patio of Stern Hall: This is a beautiful place to get work done when the sun is out... there are really cute tables and chairs outside.

cards.title: Denny Hall First Floor Corners

cards.notes: Find a pillowy sofa in a cozy corner on the first floor of Denny Hall for a quiet, focused environment away from campus rush.
cards.short_summary: Quiet, comfortable seating areas on the first floor of the historic Denny Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny Hall's First Floor... take a seat on a pillowy sofa in a cozy corner on the first floor of Denny Hall.
cards.source_title: Places to Study on Dickinson's Campus
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Denny Hall building hours.

cards.title: Weiss Center Art Study Hallway
cards.subtitle: Creative Corridor
cards.notes: A dedicated study hallway within the Weiss Center for the Arts, providing a quiet space surrounded by the college's art and music departments.
cards.short_summary: A specialized study hallway located within the Weiss Center for the Arts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Art and Art History Department's facilities... consist of numerous buildings and spaces: Weiss Center for the Arts... Art & Art History Study Hallway.
cards.source_title: Facilities and Resources | Dickinson College

cards.title: Stuart Hall Second Floor

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Explore the unique rituals and symbols of the first college chartered in the newly recognized United States, from mermaid lore to the sacred steps of Old West.

cards.title: The Convocation Ascent
cards.subtitle: Old West
cards.notes: Walk up the historic limestone steps of Old West during Convocation to ceremonially sign into the college as a first-year student.
cards.short_summary: First-year students ascend the Old West steps during Convocation to sign the college's matriculation book.
cards.evidence_claim: During Convocation, new students walk up the steps, through the doors into Memorial Hall and sign into the college.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during the Convocation ceremony in August.

cards.title: The Commencement Descent
cards.subtitle: Old West
cards.notes: Exit through the doors of Old West and descend the stone steps as a graduate, a tradition held since 1967.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors descend the Old West steps during Commencement to symbolize their transition to alumni.
cards.evidence_claim: At Commencement, the graduating class walks out the doors and down the steps, symbolically exiting the college.
cards.source_title: Old West Then and Now | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during the Commencement ceremony in May.

cards.title: The Unexpected Mermaid
cards.subtitle: Old West Cupola
cards.notes: Look for the mermaid atop Old West, a coppersmith's 1803 mistake that became the college's most beloved symbol.
cards.short_summary: A mermaid weathervane, originally intended to be Triton, serves as a primary symbol of Dickinson College.
cards.evidence_claim: The local metalworker created a mermaid instead of the requested Triton; the original is now in the library while a replica is on Old West.
cards.source_title: The Mermaid Story | Archives & Special Collections - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: The replica is visible atop Old West; the original is displayed in the Waidner-Spahr Library.

cards.title: Don't Step on the Seal
cards.subtitle: Britton Plaza
cards.notes: Avoid treading on the bronze college seal embedded in Britton Plaza to ensure you graduate on time.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition warns that stepping on the college seal in Britton Plaza prevents graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: Legend has it that if a student treads on the college seal embedded in the middle of Britton Plaza, he or she won't graduate.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: The seal is located outdoors in the center of Britton Plaza.

cards.title: The Cafsgiving Feast
cards.subtitle: Holland Union Building
cards.notes: Join the campus community for a Thanksgiving meal served by college administrators and staff in the dining hall.
cards.short_summary: Cafsgiving is an annual communal Thanksgiving dinner where staff serve students.
cards.evidence_claim: Every year, the campus community gathers for Cafsgiving, a communal Thanksgiving meal served by college staff and administrators.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Held annually in November before Thanksgiving break.

cards.title: Charter Day Celebration
cards.subtitle: Old West Lawn
cards.notes: Celebrate the 1783 signing of the college charter with an annual picnic and philanthropy events on September 9.
cards.short_summary: Charter Day commemorates the founding of Dickinson College with campus-wide festivities.
cards.evidence_claim: Charter Day commemorates the signing of the college's charter in 1783 and celebrates philanthropy at Dickinson.
cards.source_title: The Tradition of Charter Day
cards.access_notes: Held annually on or near September 9.

cards.title: The Red Devil's Moxie
cards.subtitle: Biddle Field
cards.notes: Cheer for the Red Devil, a mascot named in 1930 after a sportswriter praised the football team's grit.
cards.short_summary: The Red Devil is the official mascot of Dickinson College, originating from a 1930 football game.
cards.evidence_claim: A Washington writer dubbed the Dickinson team “the Red Devils” in 1930 because of their grit against George Washington University.
cards.source_title: The Dawn of the Red Devil | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Appears at athletic events and campus celebrations.

cards.title: The Tapping Ceremonies
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide
cards.notes: Watch the annual spring tapping ceremonies where students are inducted into honorary societies like Raven's Claw.
cards.short_summary: Dickinson's honorary 'hat societies' tap new members each spring based on leadership and academics.
cards.evidence_claim: Each spring brings members of the community together for tapping ceremonies for honorary societies known as “hat societies.”
cards.source_title: Hats Off! | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Ceremonies take place at various campus locations in the spring.

cards.title: Wearing the Red and White
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide
cards.notes: Sport the college colors derived from the 18th-century Belles Lettres and Union Philosophical literary societies.
cards.short_summary: Dickinson's red and white colors originate from its two oldest student literary societies.
cards.evidence_claim: The official red and white colors emerged from the societies' symbols: a red rose for Belles Lettres and a white rose for UPS.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Celebrated during 'Wear the Red Fridays' and athletic events.

cards.title: The Global Directional Sign
cards.subtitle: Old West Lawn
cards.notes: Check the signpost in front of Old West that points toward Dickinson's global study centers around the world.
cards.short_summary: A directional signpost highlights Dickinson's commitment to international education.
cards.evidence_claim: The directional sign located in front of Old West shows these global connections by pointing to Dickinson centers around the world.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Located on the lawn in front of Old West.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Dickinson College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Unpack and Meet Your Floor
cards.subtitle: Wednesday Morning Move-In
cards.notes: Start your journey by moving into your residence hall. Meet your Resident Advisor and neighbors during the first floor meeting at 2:00 PM to kick off orientation.
cards.short_summary: The official start of the first-year experience begins with residential move-in and floor meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: New Student Move-in occurs from 8-11 AM on Wednesday, followed by a First Floor Meeting in Residence Halls from 2-3 PM.
cards.source_title: Move-In and Orientation Schedule - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Restricted to residential students and their families during move-in hours.

cards.title: Grab Info and Swag
cards.subtitle: Wednesday Information Tents
cards.notes: Head to the center of campus to visit information tents. It is the best spot to ask questions and get your bearings before the formal ceremonies begin.
cards.short_summary: Britton Plaza serves as the central hub for information and campus navigation during orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: All college information tents are located at Britton Plaza from 10 AM to 12 PM on the first day of orientation.
cards.source_title: Move-In and Orientation Schedule - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Open public plaza in the heart of campus.

cards.title: Join the Welcome Night
cards.subtitle: Wednesday Evening Social
cards.notes: Gather on the grass for Welcome Night. This large-scale social event is designed for the entire incoming class to mingle and celebrate their arrival.
cards.short_summary: Morgan Field hosts the primary evening social event for new students on their first night.
cards.evidence_claim: Welcome Night is held on Morgan Field from 7-9 PM on the first Wednesday of orientation.
cards.source_title: Move-In and Orientation Schedule - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor field accessible to all students.

cards.title: Attend the Hype Session
cards.subtitle: Thursday Morning Kickoff
cards.notes: Start your second day with high energy at the ATS. This session transitions you from social move-in to the academic expectations of the college.
cards.short_summary: The ATS auditorium is the venue for large-scale student assemblies and orientation hype sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: A Welcome/Hype Session is scheduled at ATS from 8:30-9:30 AM on the Thursday of orientation week.
cards.source_title: Move-In and Orientation Schedule - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Indoor auditorium used for major campus events.

cards.title: Sign Into the College
cards.subtitle: Sunday Convocation Tradition
cards.notes: Walk up the historic stone steps of Old West to sign the college ledger. This tradition officially marks your entry into the Dickinson community.
cards.short_summary: The 'Signing In' ceremony at Old West is a foundational tradition for every new Dickinson student.
cards.evidence_claim: During Convocation, new students walk up the stone steps of Old West and sign into the college in Memorial Hall.
cards.source_title: Dickinson Officially Welcomes the Class of 2029 at Convocation
cards.access_notes: The doors of Old West are opened specifically for this ceremony.

cards.title: Share a Welcome Meal
cards.subtitle: Daily Orientation Dining
cards.notes: Head to 'The Caf' for a meal with your New Student Guide. It is the primary spot to refuel and meet classmates between orientation sessions.
cards.short_summary: The main dining hall in the HUB is the central location for orientation meals and student gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Welcome Lunch and 'Meet and Eat' sessions with New Student Guides are held at the Dining Hall.
cards.source_title: Hours of Operations and Highlights | Dining Hall - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Requires a meal swipe or payment for entry.

cards.title: Explore Your Study Hub
cards.subtitle: Academic Resource Tour
cards.notes: Visit the library to learn about research resources. It's open late on Sundays, making it a key spot for preparing for your first Monday classes.
cards.short_summary: Waidner-Spahr Library provides critical academic support and late-night study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The library is open until 12 AM on Sundays during the academic semester.
cards.source_title: Library Hours | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Dickinson ID required after 5 PM for entry.

cards.title: Active Break at Kline
cards.subtitle: Weekend Recreation
cards.notes: Take a break from orientation meetings with a workout. The fitness center offers weekend hours for students to stay active before classes start.
cards.short_summary: The Kline Center is the primary facility for student fitness, recreation, and intramural sports.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kline Fitness Center is open on Saturdays from 9 AM - 7 PM and Sundays from 12 PM - 10:30 PM.
cards.source_title: Kline Fitness Center - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students with a valid Dickinson ID.

cards.title: Coffee at The Quarry
cards.subtitle: Weekend Social Hangout
cards.notes: Visit this reimagined campus hangout for a locally roasted coffee. It is a favorite spot for students to socialize in a relaxed, historic setting.
cards.short_summary: The Quarry is a central campus social space featuring Denim Coffee and student meeting areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Denim Coffee at the Quarry is open seven days a week from 7:30 AM to 3 PM.
cards.source_title: Dickinson Welcomes Denim Coffee at the Quarry
cards.access_notes: Open to the public and students daily.

cards.title: Movie Night Downtown
cards.subtitle: Saturday Night Out
cards.notes: Walk a few blocks into downtown Carlisle for a movie. The college often partners with this historic theatre for free student screenings during opening week.
cards.short_summary: The Carlisle Theatre is a historic venue downtown that hosts community and student film events.
cards.evidence_claim: Orientation events have included free screenings for students at the Carlisle Theatre (40 W. High St).
cards.source_title: Welcome Class of 2024 | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Located downtown; specific orientation screenings are free for students.
